description_full: LifeStance Health Group, Inc., through its subsidiaries, provides outpatient mental health services to children, adolescents, adults, and geriatrics in the United States. The company offers patients a multidisciplinary suite of mental health services, psychiatric evaluations and treatment, psychological, and neuropsychological testing, as well as individual, family, and group therapy. It also treats a range of mental health conditions, including anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, eating disorders, psychotic disorders, and post-traumatic stress disorder. In addition, the company operates an outpatient mental health platform, as well as offers patient care virtually through its online delivery platform or in-person at its centers. LifeStance Health Group, Inc. was founded in 2017 and is headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona.

financial_summary: LifeStance Health Group, Inc. is a mid-cap healthcare business with a $5.2B market cap on $1.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +18% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +11.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -10% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $110M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 15.12× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.5× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 2.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 3.1% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
